■ The ones that kept runs going: fallback, recovery and maintenance. Not healing.

All in one suite. End to end.

Identification Was a Fallback Ladder

1Normal identification — the recorded properties
2Smart Identification — not found? try other properties
3Index-based — identical objects? use position
4Image-based — properties won't help? match what you see (Insight, 11.5+)
Still failing? Recovery Scenario / Maintenance Mode

When a Step Failed, QTP Didn't Just Stop

Recovery Scenarios

Failure detected
↓
Run an alternate action
↓
Retry only the failed step, continue

Maintenance Mode

Object not found
↓
A person updates the object, guided
↓
Continue the same run

Plus Update Run: one run mode to refresh object descriptions and expected values.

Recovery takes another path. Maintenance needs a person. Neither is healing.

What Should a Test Do When It Breaks?

STOP

"I don't know what happened."

GUESS

"This element looks similar."

REASON

"I understand the intent. Let me work out what changed."

Shouldn't intelligent automation be able to reason?

Locator Is Not Intent

INTENT

Click Login

The test intent tells us WHAT.

IMPLEMENTATION

#lgnbtn

The locator tells us HOW.

The application can change. The intent may not.

Test step

If the test has all this context, why can't it reason about its own failure?

Healing or Not? You Decide

A step fails. Then this happens. Is it healing?

Playwright runs the whole failed test again
RETRY
A try/catch clicks Cancel and the test moves on
RECOVERY
Smart Identification tries other recorded properties
FALLBACK
After the failure, an agent edits the locator in the test file
MAINTENANCE
During the run, the step finds Sign In by its intent, continues, and reports it
HEALING ✅

What Is Healing, What Is Not

WhenWhat happensExamples
Retry / waitDuring the runThe whole test again, or the same step until it times outPlaywright test retries; auto-wait
RecoveryDuring the runAnother path; the step itself is not fixedQTP Recovery Scenarios, try/catch
FallbackDuring the runAlternatives written in advanceQTP Smart Identification, locator lists
HealingDuring the runFinds the element that matches the step's intent on today's page, continues, explainsThis talk
MaintenanceAfter the runThe test code is changedA person, QTP Maintenance Mode, Playwright Healer agent
VerificationAfter maintenanceThe test runs again with healing offProves the change holds

Healing happens during the run. Changing the code afterwards is maintenance.

Runtime healing doesn't hide defects. It uncovers the ones a broken locator was hiding.

Why Do We Need Runtime Healing?

After the run (e.g. Playwright Healer agent)During the run
The rest of the testNever ranRuns, so defects behind the break are found
Three breaks in one flowThree fix-and-rerun cyclesOne run, one pull request
Decision made onA recreated pageThe real page, in its real state
The pipelineRed; the release waitsJudged on what the application does

A post-run healer fixes the test. Runtime healing saves the run.

You need both: heal during the run, then fix the code and prove it after.

45Apply the Heal, Then Prove It

APPLY HEAL

src/pages/loginpage.ts:11
- this.txtUserName = page.getByPlaceholder("Username1")
+ this.txtUserName = page.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Username" })

Preview the change first. Never auto-commit.

VERIFY WITHOUT HEALING

Healing OFF

Otherwise the AI could simply rescue the test again.

The test passes because the test code was fixed, not because healing intervened.

The Moment of Truth

The fix is applied. Healing is off. Will it pass?

Healing DISABLED
# re-run the fixed tests, healing disabled npx playwright test login.spec.ts ✓ login test

VERIFIED

Now we know the test itself was repaired.

Healing DISABLED
# same run, the fix did not hold npx playwright test login.spec.ts ✘ login test

NOT VERIFIED

PR labelled "verification FAILED" · CI job fails · a human decides.

The objective isn't to make every test green. It's to make automation more intelligent and trustworthy.

Recover Without Hiding Defects

Risks, Limits, and the Answer

How can self-healing automation recover from failures without hiding real application defects?

Healing Alone vs Verified Healing

HEALING ALONE

"I found a way to continue."

VERIFIED HEALING

"I changed the test and proved it works without healing."

Where AI can go wrong without verification:

Wrong elementIncorrect assumptionHidden app defectFalse healingOverhealingWrong permanent change

Self healing without verification creates false confidence.

What Healing Must Never Touch

HEAL: ACTIONS

  • Click, fill, check, select
  • Read values: text, attributes, state
  • Inside frames, popups and new tabs

NEVER HEAL

  • Assertions (expect): "fixing" one hides a real bug
  • Waits (waitFor): a timeout can be the right answer

Healing changes how a test finds an element. Never what the test checks.

The Answer

How can self-healing automation recover from failures without hiding real application defects?

1
Heal actions only. Never assertions or waits.
2
Heal by intent. The accessibility tree first, then the DOM, then the page image.
3
Change how an element is found, never what the test checks. A real defect still fails.
4
Show every heal. What broke, what changed, where, and whether it needs review.
5
Verify with healing off, and let a person decide in a pull request.
6
Don't force a heal. When the case is complex, let the test fail and write every finding in the report for review after the run.

Recover the step. Never hide the defect.

Don't aim for 100% autonomy. Reliability matters more than healing.

From Tests That Run to Tests That Evolve

Tests that run
They execute what we wrote.
Tests that heal
They keep running when the app changes.
📍 You are here
Tests that evolve
They keep up with what the app becomes.

Are we building tests that test our applications…
…or tests that can evolve with them?

Beyond Healing

Self Evolving Test Automation

A self-healing suite survives change. A self-evolving suite keeps up with it.

Release 2.0: What Should the Suite Do?

Four changes ship together. Decide for each one.

Login is renamed Sign In
→
Heal it during the run, then propose the fix as a pull request
Sign in with SSO is added
→
An exploring agent finds the new flow and drafts a test
Remember me is removed
→
The run flags it; exploration confirms it's gone
The cart total is wrong
→
Report a likely product defect. Do not heal.

Only one of the four is healing. The rest is the suite evolving.

How a Suite Evolves

A run only sees the pages its tests already visit. Evolving needs two sources.

What the run sees · known pages

  • Remember: a fix applied once is never healed again
  • Classify: drift, change, defect, flaky, environment
  • Flag: a test whose intent is gone, for review

What an agent explores · new pages

  • Grow: finds new flows and drafts tests from verified interactions
  • Confirm: a feature is really gone before its test retires

Both arrive as suggestions in a pull request. A person approves. Evolution without review is drift.

Key Takeaways

1
Heal during the run, maintain after it. You need both.
2
Recover the step, never hide the defect. Heal actions only, and verify with healing off.
3
Evolve with suggestions, not autonomy. A person approves; reliability matters more than healing.

The future of test automation isn't automation that never fails.
It's automation that knows what to do when it does.
